sourceLine: your VR training analytics and the questions safety managers ask before they trust a VR certificate

cards.title: Measuring Transfer, Not Completion
cards.angle: A March 2026 Scientific Reports study compared VR-trained substation workers against observations at a real site, and the field is starting to ask for that kind of evidence instead of completion rates. Your LMS already captures the inputs; the measurement guide is missing.
cards.evidence: Your analytics page logs actions, decisions, accuracy and timing per trainee, while your Komatsu case reports a potential 55.13 percent time-efficiency saving per class for the 2022 cohort, a throughput figure. The article is how to turn logged decisions into a transfer measure a safety manager trusts.

sources.title: Virtual reality to enhance risk management and safety in electrical substations

cards.title: What a VR Training Record Should Contain
cards.angle: WA mining statutory role holders face new competency and examination criteria from March 30 2026. A certificate from a VR LMS is only evidence if an assessor can see what was tested, how and when.
cards.evidence: Your LMS issues certificates and exports data in multiple formats to a client LMS but names no SCORM or xAPI standard. The piece defines the fields a defensible record needs and where exports fall short.

cards.title: Headset Fleets After Quest for Business
cards.angle: Meta stopped selling commercial Quest SKUs and new managed-services subscriptions on February 20 2026, with existing customers supported to January 2030. Any fleet standing up now is consumer hardware plus third-party MDM.
cards.evidence: Your pricing page lists seven supported headsets across Meta and Pico while your FAQ names only two Pico devices, and offline mode is gated to the top tier. A fleet-ops guide for remote sites would resolve the inconsistency and answer the first question a mine site IT lead asks.

sources.title: Meta Quest for Business Ends: What It Means for VR Training
